### Added
- **`networkPolicy.mcpBackends`: an in-cluster MCP backend reachable only through muster.** A backend an installation registers with muster behind a ClusterIP admits every pod on the cluster unless something restricts it, and a direct call skips muster's sign-in, audit trail and toolset scoping. Each entry (`namespace`, `ports`, optional `podSelector`, `metrics`, `additionalPeers`) renders `agent-platform-connectivity-mcp-backend-<key>` in the backend's namespace, in the resolved flavour: on the entry's ports it admits muster from the release namespace, `networkPolicy.mcpBackendScrapers` when `metrics: true` (default: alloy-metrics in `kube-system`) and the entry's `additionalPeers` (e.g. the gateway in front of a backend with a public route); on every port it admits the namespace's own pods; in the cilium flavour it also admits the kubelet's probes (the host entity) on every port, since a backend may probe on another port than it serves. It is the ingress counterpart of `networkPolicy.musterInClusterMcpPorts`. `make verify-mcp-backend-netpol` asserts both flavours, and that nothing renders without entries or with `networkPolicy.enabled: false`.
